description: Project Eric OWASP Top 10 (2021) scanner rule pack. Reads as JSON; the structure mirrors the OWASP categories, and the `languages` array carries language-specific extensions of the global rules.

A01.name: Broken Access Control
A01.description: Authorization enforced by the UI is bypassed, or missing on routes that take user-supplied ids.

A02.name: Cryptographic Failures
A02.description: Weak, missing, or misused cryptography. Includes storing passwords in cleartext, weak hashing (MD5/SHA1), and using HTTP where TLS is available.

A03.name: Injection
A03.description: User-controlled input is interpreted as code, a query, or a command. SQL injection, command injection, XSS, and template injection all fall here.

A04.name: Insecure Design
A04.description: A control or process is missing by design. Can't be fixed by better implementation — it has to be redesigned.

A05.name: Security Misconfiguration
A05.description: Default credentials, debug flags enabled in production, verbose error pages, missing patches, and unprotected files.

A06.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
A06.description: Using libraries with known vulnerabilities, or components that are no longer maintained.

A07.name: Identification and Authentication Failures
A07.description: Authentication is broken — weak passwords, no MFA, credential stuffing, exposed session tokens.

A08.name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
A08.description: Code or data is assumed trustworthy without verifying its integrity. CI/CD pipelines without integrity verification, deserialisation from untrusted input, auto-update without signature verification.

A09.name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
A09.description: Insufficient logging, missing alerts, and inability to investigate or respond to incidents.

A10.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
A10.description: Server fetches a remote URL based on user input without validating the destination — enabling access to internal services.

globalRules.name: Weak hash algorithm (MD5)
globalRules.summary: MD5 is cryptographically broken. Use SHA-256 or stronger.
globalRules.description: MD5 has known collision attacks. Use sha256 or sha3-256 instead. For passwords, use bcrypt, scrypt, or argon2.

fix.title: Replace MD5 with SHA-256
fix.hint: Use SHA-256 or stronger. For password hashing, use bcrypt/scrypt/argon2.

globalRules.name: Weak hash algorithm (SHA-1)
globalRules.summary: SHA-1 is deprecated. Use SHA-256 or stronger.
globalRules.description: SHA-1 has known collision attacks (SHAttered, 2017). Modern systems should use SHA-256 or stronger.

fix.title: Replace SHA-1 with SHA-256
fix.hint: Use SHA-256, SHA-3, or BLAKE2. For HMAC, use HMAC-SHA256.

globalRules.name: Hard-coded credential
globalRules.summary: A password, API key, or secret is hard-coded in the source. Anyone with repo access can read it.
globalRules.description: Secrets in source code end up in version control, build artifacts, and crash dumps. Move them to environment variables or a secrets manager.

fix.title: Move the secret to environment variables
fix.hint: Read it from process.env at runtime. Use a secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Doppler) in production.

globalRules.name: Insecure HTTP URL
globalRules.summary: A plain HTTP URL is used where HTTPS is available.
globalRules.description: Plain HTTP traffic is unauthenticated and unencrypted. A network attacker can read or modify the request.

fix.title: Switch to HTTPS
fix.hint: Replace http:// with https://. For local development, localhost is fine.

globalRules.name: SQL string concatenation
globalRules.summary: SQL is built by concatenating user input — classic SQL injection.
globalRules.description: User-controlled input concatenated into a SQL string lets an attacker modify the query (UNION SELECT, DROP TABLE, etc). Use parameterised queries or an ORM.

fix.title: Use parameterised queries
fix.hint: Replace string concatenation with placeholders (? or :name) and pass user input as parameters.

globalRules.name: Command injection (exec/system)
globalRules.summary: User input flows into exec/system/popen — classic command injection.
globalRules.description: User input passed to a shell command lets the attacker run arbitrary OS commands. Avoid shell execution or sanitise the input through a strict allowlist.

fix.title: Avoid shell execution of user input
fix.hint: Pass arguments as an array (no shell). Sanitise against a strict allowlist if the input must be used in a command.

globalRules.name: Cross-site scripting (innerHTML)
globalRules.summary: innerHTML is being assigned — high risk of XSS.
globalRules.description: Assigning user-controlled strings to innerHTML lets attackers inject script tags. Use textContent or a sanitiser such as DOMPurify.

fix.title: Use textContent or DOMPurify
fix.hint: Use element.textContent for plain text, or a sanitiser like DOMPurify for HTML.

globalRules.name: eval() on user input
globalRules.summary: eval() executes arbitrary code. Never pass user input to it.
globalRules.description: eval() executes its argument as code. Anything an attacker can influence becomes arbitrary code execution in your process.

fix.title: Avoid eval()
fix.hint: Replace with a safer alternative (JSON.parse, a parser, a lookup table).

globalRules.name: TODO/FIXME without security review
globalRules.description: Code that handles auth, secrets, payments, or user data with TODO/FIXME may not be production-ready.

fix.title: Resolve the TODO before shipping
fix.hint: Replace the marker with a complete implementation or remove the dead code path.

globalRules.name: CORS wildcard
globalRules.summary: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * allows any origin to read responses.
globalRules.description: A wildcard CORS policy combined with credentials or sensitive responses enables cross-origin theft.

fix.title: Lock CORS to known origins
fix.hint: List the exact origins that should be allowed. Never combine * with credentials.

globalRules.name: Debug mode in code
globalRules.description: Debug mode exposes stack traces, configuration, and sometimes the REPL. Disable it in production.

fix.title: Disable debug mode in production
fix.hint: Set DEBUG = False (or use a config-driven flag) before deploying.

globalRules.name: Weak password validation
globalRules.summary: Password length check is too short (< 6).
globalRules.description: Most security guidance requires at least 8–12 characters. Enforce length and complexity on the server side.

fix.title: Require ≥ 8 character passwords
fix.hint: NIST SP 800-63B recommends ≥ 8 characters. Enforce on the server side.

globalRules.name: Plaintext password storage
globalRules.description: Plaintext passwords in storage expose every user when the database leaks. Always hash with bcrypt/scrypt/argon2.

fix.title: Hash passwords with bcrypt/scrypt/argon2
fix.hint: Never store passwords in plaintext or with reversible encryption.

globalRules.name: Pickle / unsafe deserialisation
globalRules.summary: Python pickle.loads / yaml.load on untrusted data is unsafe.
globalRules.description: pickle and yaml.load can execute arbitrary code when given malicious input. Use json, or yaml.safe_load.

fix.title: Use a safe deserialiser
fix.hint: Use json or yaml.safe_load. pickle should only be used for trusted, internal data.

globalRules.name: SSRF — request to user URL
globalRules.summary: Server makes an HTTP request to a user-supplied URL.
globalRules.description: When the server fetches a URL from user input without validation, the user can reach internal services (169.254.169.254 cloud metadata, 127.0.0.1, file://, etc).

fix.title: Validate URLs against an allowlist
fix.hint: Block private IP ranges (RFC 1918, link-local 169.254.0.0/16, loopback 127.0.0.0/8). Use a service-side proxy if you must accept arbitrary URLs.

rules.name: Math.random used for security
rules.description: Math.random uses a non-cryptographic PRNG. Use crypto.getRandomValues or crypto.randomUUID for security-sensitive operations.

fix.title: Use crypto.getRandomValues() instead
fix.hint: For tokens or session ids, use crypto.randomUUID() or crypto.getRandomValues() with a Uint8Array.

rules.name: document.write after user data
rules.summary: document.write with dynamic input can lead to XSS.
rules.description: Writing user-controlled data into the document with document.write can inject script tags. Use safer DOM APIs.

fix.title: Use safe DOM APIs
fix.hint: Use textContent, setAttribute, or insertAdjacentHTML with sanitised content.

rules.name: any in security-sensitive code
rules.summary: Using `any` defeats TypeScript's type checks for security-sensitive values.
rules.description: When a security-sensitive value (request input, JWT payload) is typed as `any`, type checks provide no protection.

fix.title: Use a precise type
fix.hint: Replace `as any` with a precise type (zod schema, interface, branded type).

rules.name: assert used for security check
rules.summary: assert can be stripped with python -O. Don't use it for security.
rules.description: Python's -O flag strips assertions. Use an explicit if/raise for security checks.

fix.title: Replace assert with explicit check
fix.hint: if not is_valid(x): raise ValueError(...)

rules.name: shell=True in subprocess
rules.summary: subprocess with shell=True passes the command to /bin/sh — vulnerable to injection.
rules.description: shell=True lets attackers break out of the command. Pass arguments as a list with shell=False.

fix.title: Pass args as a list, shell=False
fix.hint: subprocess.run(['ls', user_input], shell=False). Validate user_input against an allowlist if you must pass it to a shell.

rules.name: Dynamic SQL identifier interpolation
rules.summary: A column or table name is interpolated into a query string.
rules.description: Most databases don't allow parameterised identifiers. Validate the identifier against an allowlist of expected names.

fix.title: Validate identifiers against an allowlist
fix.hint: Keep a known-good list of columns/tables and check the user input against it.

fix.title: Switch to SHA-256
fix.hint: MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")

rules.name: Unsanitised $_GET / $_POST echoed
rules.description: Echoing request input directly lets attackers inject script. Use htmlspecialchars($x, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8').

fix.title: Sanitise with htmlspecialchars
fix.hint: echo htmlspecialchars($x, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8');

rules.name: math/rand used for crypto
rules.description: Use crypto/rand for security-sensitive random values (tokens, nonces, session ids).

fix.title: Use crypto/rand instead
fix.hint: n, err := rand.Read(buf) — package crypto/rand

rules.name: unwrap() on user input
rules.summary: unwrap() on parsed user input will panic — DoS risk.
rules.description: Always handle parse errors gracefully on user-controlled data.

fix.title: Use ? operator or match
fix.hint: let n: u32 = s.parse()?;

rules.name: ERB template from user input
rules.summary: Rendering ERB with user-controlled templates enables RCE.
rules.description: Never pass user input directly to ERB.new. Use a safe templating engine or a whitelist.

fix.title: Sanitise templates before rendering
fix.hint: Validate against an allowlist, or strip ERB tags from user input.

rules.name: strcpy / strcat on dynamic buffer
rules.summary: strcpy/strcat ignore buffer size — classic buffer overflow.
rules.description: Use strncpy, strncat, or std::string. Better: use modern C++ containers.

fix.title: Use bounded string functions
fix.hint: strncpy(dst, src, sizeof(dst) - 1); dst[sizeof(dst) - 1] = '\0';

rules.name: MD5CryptoServiceProvider
rules.description: Use SHA256CryptoServiceProvider or, for passwords, Rfc2898DeriveBytes (PBKDF2).

fix.title: Switch to SHA-256 or PBKDF2
fix.hint: SHA256.Create() or new Rfc2898DeriveBytes(password, salt, iterations)

rules.name: Missing Content-Security-Policy meta
rules.summary: No Content-Security-Policy meta tag in the HTML.
rules.description: CSP provides defence-in-depth against XSS by restricting what scripts can run.

fix.title: Add a Content-Security-Policy meta tag
fix.hint: <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'">
